items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — opened straight into 'How can I help you today?'
No time expectation or 'Sound good?' confirmation on the agenda — she outlined the plan ('create your profile... then transfer you to a moving specialist') but never asked the customer to confirm it
No recap of an existing record — the customer had already been quoted ($104/mover/hr, $151 travel fee) but the rep said 'let me create your profile here,' treating a returning lead as a fresh intake
Probe gaps: never asked about garage/storage rooms, box count, storage stops, additional stops, special considerations (long walks, narrow hallways), parking/HOA/access, or moving stressors
No confirmation-email handoff explained — only a text message with the walkthrough link; no bolded-details list, no 'reply with any corrections'
Never asked 'Any other questions before I let you go?'
Customer's name used only twice ('Hey, Melanie' / 'you do the same, Melanie') — 'ma'am' carried the rest of the call

Muddled middle: offered a vague 'she'll call you back in about ten to fifteen minutes,' then pushed back on the customer's preferred timing, and the customer had to steer the conversation twice before a walkthrough slot got locked in
Introduced herself as 'Arlene' on a call logged to Jeline Lavarias — worth confirming whether that is an approved floor name
top_strength: Clean, accurate intake under time pressure at the end of the day — she captured both addresses with zips and spellings, both home sizes, single-level status at origin and destination, the two-day pack-and-move dates, and confirmed the customer's previously quoted rates were accurate. She also closed with a concrete, unambiguous next step: Friday 10:00 AM, text link, click it and someone joins by video.
coaching_note: Book the walkthrough on the first ask instead of routing to a callback. When Melanie said she wasn't free today, Jeline's first move was 'I'll ask her to give you a call back in ten to fifteen minutes' — an open loop with no owner. Melanie then had to redirect twice ('when she calls back I can schedule a video call,' 'could you schedule the call for she and I') before Jeline offered to book it herself. She had the calendar the whole time. The rule: if the customer can't do the walkthrough now, immediately offer two concrete slots and lock one. That also avoids the pressure line she reached for ('that date might book out') which read as friction rather than urgency.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and pleasant with real warmth in spots ('good afternoon honey,' 'that's alright,' 'thank you for spelling that out') and the customer closed happily, but the call leaned transactional — heavy 'Mm-hmm' filler, 'ma'am' in place of her name, and no acknowledgment of the customer's apology for calling late in the day.
